citations.text: Efklides, A., & Schwartz, B. L. (2024). Revisiting the Metacognitive and Affective Model of Self-Regulated Learning: Origins, Development, and Future Directions. Educational Psychology Review, 36, 61.

en.general: The relatively stable things a learner brings to any learning situation: prior knowledge, metacognitive knowledge and skills, beliefs about ability, effort, value and cost, other motivations, and attitudes and emotions toward learning. Goal setting before the work begins is shaped here.

examples: A student's belief that effort pays off.
A student's anxiety about mathematics in general.
nonExamples: A feeling of difficulty during one problem.
